newsitem.title: INDIA: India's L&T mulls cement terminals on west coast.
newsitem.headline: India's L&T mulls cement terminals on west coast.

text.p: India's second largest cement maker, Larsen and Toubro Ltd (L&T), said it plans to install receiving terminals at some west coast ports to speed cement distribution from its Gujarat plant.

L&T managing director Sudhakar Kulkarni told Reuters in a recent interview that the firm had built a port at its Gujarat cement plant in order to ship cement to other states along the western coastal strand.

"One advantage of this Gujarat plant is that it is a coast- based plant," Kulkarni said. "We are about 2.5-to-three km away from the sea. So we have built our own port, where a 45,000 tonne ship can be berthed."
L&T is currently in the process of doubling the capacity of its Gujarat cement plant to around four million tonnes annually, Kulkarni said.

"Our idea on this plant is to export cement to neighbouring countries as well as to cater to the western coastal market," Kulkarni added. "We'll be doing it on the coast at places like Surat for instance, or bring it to Bombay. We'll go to Mangalore, Cochin, Sri Lanka..."
He said the firm planned to build receiving terminals at some of these ports, but had not crystallised the details.
"If necessary we'll build terminals. We have plans in some of these places to build some. We're working on it but that will be long-term, this may not be immediate."
Kulkarni said the terminals would not be very large. "The local demand can't be very large, and requirements will be such that a ship can go periodically. It won't be very large."

L&T recently announced a net profit of 4.11 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, up from 3.89 billion in the previous year, with cement production rising 42 percent to 5.4 million tonnes in 1996/97 against 3.8 million tonnes the previous year.
